title: UX-01 task 8: the Babylon table scene and its semantic overlay
actor: Claude Code agent (architect/QA reviewer role) on Director request, local WSL session

changes.description: Implementation-plan task 8 (decision D27, design 'Babylon table scene'): packages/presentation/src/table-scene.ts adds mountTableScene(canvas, input, options) returning update, cardRects, dispose and a frame count, with validateTableInput and layoutTable. Closed input is validated before anything is created; layout is deterministic; the camera is fixed about 22 degrees from top-down; zone surfaces, key light, soft fill and contact shadows; unlit card art from thumbnails; exerted cards and locations turned; Shift stacks offset; face-down inkwell, deck and opponent hand with the card back; outline frames in the focus colour for selection and targets. It renders on demand only (after mount and update once materials are ready, and after resize), takes no input or focus, and disposes everything on failure or dispose().

Design system: SceneOverlay (Experimental) places one React Aria button per board object at the projected rectangle, at least 44 px, with text markers below, or above for the far side; describeBoardCard is extracted from BoardCard so the overlay and the Flat tier share names and markers; component token match.scene-min. packages/design-system gains the development-only workspace dependency @lorcana/presentation (pnpm-lock adds one importer link). stories/support/reference/scene.tsx lazily loads the scene, maps the position, renderer colours and card back into its input, recomputes rectangles on resize, falls back to the Flat tier with an explanation on engine, texture or context failure, and uses the Flat tier below 80 rem. Match stories add the table scene, scene with targets, renderer failure and scene takedown.

Six NullEngine tests in packages/presentation/tests/table-scene.test.mjs (validation refusals, layout, on-demand frames, projection, disposal, engine failure), written alongside the implementation rather than captured failing first; four scene browser tests in reference.spec.ts. RUN-20261022-035 failed 6 of 409 on axe aria-hidden-focus (Babylon's input handling set a tab index on the decorative canvas) and is preserved; after detaching input RUN-20261022-036 and RUN-20261022-037 pass (presentation and boundaries; gates and 409/409 Chromium tests).

Visual review found a blank first scene (on-demand frames before shaders compiled; now rendered after whenReadyAsync), colliding overlay markers (now card-width, hyphenated, above far-side cards, with wider row spacing) and illegible markers at 1180 px (Flat tier below 80 rem). Paper and Ink captures are in the ignored .local/ux-01-review/; the scene's look is a human review because Chromium renders WebGL in software.
Presentation README, F-RENDERER (features register and FEATURES.md), design-system runbook (table scene) and validation (task 8), handoff.
